projection_source.behavior: Native casts attention result to input dtype, reshapes B,S,H,d to B,S,H*d, then o_proj.
Linear gathers compute weight and uses ...i,oi->...o with explicit output sharding.
Legacy flattens KV/group into named heads only, casts dtype, calls named o_proj; head_size remains a separate named contracted dimension.
Named Linear contracts input axes with scaled weight through NamedArray.dot; result auto-sharded.

equation: dW[o,h*d+k] = sum_b,sum_s G[b,s,o]*X[b,h,s,k]. Native transposes/reshapes X to[b,s,h*d+k]; legacy retains h,k as output axes. Both are mathematically the same contraction over B,S, with DEFAULT precision and BF16 output.
static_differences: Legacy StableHLO VJP contracts BF16 G[8,2048,2048] with X[8,16,2048,128] over[0,1]x[0,2], yielding BF16[2048,16,128]. Native contracts BF16 G[8,2048,2048] with Xflat[8,2048,2048] over[0,1]x[0,1], yielding BF16[2048,2048].

Native X view is explicitly transpose[0,2,1,3] then flatten heads/head128, with P(data,None,model); G is P(data,None,None). Native VJP result is first P(None,model), then P(data,model). Legacy named path retains separate H,d dimensions and equivalent external sharding.

Optimized local legacy weight-gradient kernel takes G[4,2048,2048] and X[4,8,2048,128], emits BF16[2048,8,128], and uses convolution window size8x4,pad7_7x0_0,rhs_reversal1x0,dim_labels1fb0_10io->b0f1. Native takes G[4,2048,2048] and Xflat[4,2048,1024], emits BF16[2048,1024], and uses window size4,dim_labels0fb_0io->bf0. Both represent one model-sharded1024-wide input and local B4*S2048 contraction, but their optimized forms/physical layouts differ.

Both local outputs are BF16, then BF16 add all-reduce over identical data replica groups{{0,2},{1,3}}, then select1024 output rows to restore FSDP storage. Legacy local output layout{2,0,1} flattens to a different physical arrangement than native{1,0}; same external partitions do not imply same internal tiling.

Old8aa has the same selected native/legacy convolution shapes/window/dimension signatures; new native operation and stack IDs shift with embedding/source changes. Current first o_proj gradient metrics are exactly old; the retained static lowering difference predates the embedding patch.
